def: A processor with thousands of simple arithmetic units and very wide memory access, fast at large, regular, parallel work such as matrix multiplication.
A GPU unit that multiplies small matrix tiles in one step at low precision, which is why peak throughput is quoted per number format.
Floating-point operations per second: the rate at which a chip does arithmetic, as opposed to FLOPs, a count of operations in a job.
How many bytes per second a processor can read from and write to its main memory.
The number of floating-point operations an algorithm performs per byte it moves to or from memory.
Limited by how fast data can be moved, not by arithmetic, so extra compute capacity would not make it faster.
Limited by the speed of the arithmetic units, so more memory bandwidth would not make it faster.
A chart of attainable FLOP/s against arithmetic intensity, bounded by a sloped memory roof and a flat compute roof.
The arithmetic intensity at which the memory roof meets the compute roof, equal to peak FLOP/s divided by bandwidth.
The approximation that training a dense transformer with N parameters on D tokens costs about 6 x N x D floating-point operations.
Model FLOPs utilisation: the fraction of a chip's peak FLOP/s that useful model arithmetic actually achieves.
The intermediate results of the forward pass that the backward pass needs, whose memory grows with batch size, sequence length and depth.
